Goliath is the legendary giant of the Philistines, famous not for his own deeds but for being the unlikely victim of a shepherd boy's victory. He was a Philistine warrior from the city of Gath, belonging to a race of giants called the Anakim, standing approximately nine to ten feet tall according to the biblical account. He was heavily armed with armor and a shield, bearing a spear with an iron head that weighed six hundred shekels, making him a formidable professional soldier of the ancient world. When the Philistine and Israelite armies faced each other with King Saul commanding Israel, Goliath challenged the Israelites to single combat with winner take all. The young shepherd David, sent to bring supplies to his older brothers in the Israelite camp, volunteered to fight Goliath despite being untested in battle. David selected five smooth stones from a stream and approached Goliath with confidence in divine favor rather than human weaponry. With a single stone fired from his sling, David struck Goliath in the forehead, felling the giant. David then took Goliath's own sword and cut off his head, an act that completely demoralized the Philistine army and sent them fleeing in defeat. The victory over Goliath became the foundational achievement that made David famous throughout Israel, eventually leading to his anointing as king.
